expectations.text: GET /api/fuel response changed to ok({ rows, total }); rows is the existing list shape
expectations.evidence: Line 73: `return ok({ rows, total })`. The rows SELECT keeps the same column list (fr.*, row_to_json(v.*) as vehicles, json_build_object(...) as drivers) and ORDER BY fr.fuel_record_id DESC.

expectations.text: total is computed by a COUNT query (not rows.length) honoring the same WHERE filters as the rows query, before LIMIT/OFFSET is applied
expectations.evidence: Lines 48-50: `SELECT COUNT(*) AS count${JOINS}${where}` executed with the filter-only params, before LIMIT/OFFSET placeholders are appended. Coerced via Number(countRows[0]?.count).

expectations.text: COUNT query keeps the JOINs to vehicles/drivers/employees so search filters on joined columns (plate_number, employee names) still work
expectations.evidence: The shared JOINS block (lines 9-14) is reused verbatim in the COUNT query, so `v.plate_number`/`e.first_name`/`e.last_name` search conditions resolve. The agent's NOTES.md explicitly explains why (search references joined columns).

expectations.text: Existing filters (vehicle_id, driver_id, fuel_type, status, search, from_date, to_date) and pagination (page/pageSize -> LIMIT/OFFSET) preserved
expectations.evidence: All six filter branches preserved byte-for-byte, including `status !== 'all'`, ILIKE with `%search%`, and the `LIMIT $n OFFSET $n` gate on page && pageSize (lines 65-70).

expectations.text: All user input reaches SQL only through $n placeholders
expectations.evidence: Every filter value pushed into the params array and referenced as $1..$n; no string interpolation of request data.

expectations.text: src/services/fuel.service.js still passes page/pageSize through via buildQuery and works with the new response shape
expectations.evidence: fuel.service.js unchanged: getFuelRecords(filters) -> apiFetch(`/api/fuel${buildQuery(filters)}`); buildQuery serializes page/pageSize, and apiFetch returns the { rows, total } JSON transparently.

claims.claim: Shared WHERE builder guarantees total and rows never drift apart
claims.evidence: One `where` string and one params array built once, reused by COUNT and rows SELECT.

claims.claim: COUNT keeps joins because search references v.plate_number and employee names
claims.evidence: JOINS reused in COUNT; search clause references v.plate_number, e.first_name, e.last_name.

uncertainties: COUNT may return a string via exec_query RPC — handled with Number()
